title: Privacy concern question
author: PoemFuture4613
selftext:
Has anyone used AI to analyze / refine their model but was concerned about privacy? I find it pretty unsettling but was wondering if anyone shared the concern / had a good solution? If running a local LLM is the best solution do I have to buy a mac pro 48GB and is that even enough to run a good LLM?

Currently am using claude to help define rules and logic but would ideally want something local / safe that can do the same. It's not running crazy software or anything just kinda brainstorming with me and doing the logic for excel mostly, creating formulas and helping me sense check along the way; also parsing data and etc.

My top solutions so far are manually masking the info (using decoy inputs ) but it feels like a waste of time, and seems like a lot of work to go back and forth between real and decoy. But could be preferable to claude knowing my entire strategy. I heard [Venice.Ai](http://venice.ai/) could be good but am not familiar with it

Would really appreciate any advice here. Mostly for peace of mind, but also it would be nice to know that whatever I come up with myself is 100% mine. I'm sure you guys can relate. thank you in advance

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body:
for what you're describing, brainstorming rules, writing Excel formulas, parsing data, you don't need a big machine. a 48GB Mac runs a quantized 27-32B model comfortably, and that size handles formula writing and sense-checking logic fine. it's noticeably weaker than Claude on long messy reasoning, so expect to break questions into smaller pieces.

if you'd rather not buy hardware, the masking route works better than people expect. rename columns to col_a, col_b, scale every number by a constant you keep to yourself, and swap tickers for letters. the model only needs the structure of the problem to write a formula, not your actual levels or symbols, so it never sees anything worth stealing.

the middle option is to keep the logic chat with Claude but run anything touching your real data locally in plain Python or Excel, so the only thing that leaves your machine is the question.

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: glad it helped. if you try the masking route, test it on one old sheet first and check the numbers come back right after you unscale them.

comments.author: fleatedplutmting
comments.body:
Your concern is reasonable. If keeping the whole strategy private is a hard requirement, running a model locally with no external calls gives you more control than a cloud service imo.

I wouldn’t buy a 48GB Mac just for this yet. Try a smaller model on your current computer first, using a few Excel and logic problems you’ve already solved to see whether it’s actually good enough. Being able to run a model doesn’t mean it will match Claude’s answers.

Dummy data helps hide your inputs, but sharing all the rules can still reveal the strategy. Keep the complete logic locally and use cloud tools for isolated questions you’re comfortable sharing. I wouldn’t assume Venice solves that concern without checking exactly where the processing happens and that gets retained.

Hope that helps

replies.author: PoemFuture4613
replies.body: thanks yeah I agree the logic is the core part really; will try out a smaller model first, worst case I buy a mac. Appreciate the guidance,

comments.author: Healthy-Tension-7470
comments.body:
Careful with Venice: when you pick GPT/Claude models there, Venice itself says to assume the provider stores your content. Only its Pro-only modes are verifiable. If you stay on Claude, turn off "Help improve Claude" in Settings > Privacy so your chats aren't used for training

(I make Citenook, a Mac app that runs AI locally and can hide names and numbers before anything goes to Claude, so it does your decoy step for you.)

replies.body: thanks. I'm on windows but could you share more info about your app by chance? sounds interesting

comments.body: Just accept that they know everything about you

comments.author: Far-Manufacturer-66
comments.body:
I think your privacy concern is completely reasonable, especially if you're developing a proprietary trading strategy.

For what you're describing, I'd look at LM Studio or Ollama before buying an expensive Mac. You can run smaller language models locally, and for Excel formulas, logic checks, and brainstorming, you may not need a particularly large model.

One distinction I've been thinking about is the difference between having AI help develop a strategy and having software analyze the strategy's trading outcomes.

For the second problem, you can potentially get useful performance analysis from an ordered sequence of R-multiples without sharing your entry rules, indicators, or actual strategy code.

I'm curious: is your biggest concern exposing the underlying strategy logic, or would you also be uncomfortable uploading historical trade results to an outside analytics service?
